propositions: The lifespan shutdown drain calls queue.join() to wait for webhook-queued reviews but does not wait for reconciler reviews that execute inline in reconcile_once, causing in-flight reconciliation work to be cancelled within ~10s instead of being granted the full shutdown_drain_seconds() budget.

Any container stop outside the autodeploy path (manual restart, host reboot, rollback) kills an in-flight reconciler review with no drain, and the failure is silent because cancelled reviews emit no voter error and restarts stays 0.
The reconciler must be prevented from starting new reviews once shutdown has begun, or the drain deadline could extend indefinitely; this requires a cooperative stop signal.

The shutdown drain for both webhook queue and reconciler reviews must share a single shutdown_drain_seconds() budget to preserve the relationship with stop_grace_period (floor 1260s) and avoid exceeding it.

The drain gate must check only reconciler in-flight count via voter.in_flight_reviews(), not queue depth, because webhook reviews are already covered by queue.join() and checking a combined count would waste budget on redundant waits.
